rationale: Twelve40minute lessons separate side/ratio foundations,degree use,complementary reasoning,ratio selection,elevation/depression,actual clinometer making/calibration and both-direction use,application/source check,audit and independent assessment. Tangent is included per sourceoutcomeb;no advanced non-right-triangle/inverse-angle syllabus is inferred.
prerequisites: Decimal rounding,lengthunits and calculator degree mode
Safe ruler/protractor handling and horizontal reference
teacher_confirmation_required: Prepare accessible protractor/templates,sharp cuts/holes,short strings and blunt secured weights;approve clean safe instruments.
Fix safe stationary indoor targets above/below sight level,teacher-approved baseline and30degree calibration reference;no sun,brightlamps,roads,heightaccess or movementwhilesighting.
Observe each learner actually make/calibrate and use for both elevation/depression;retain artifact/actionlog/rawrepeatedreadings and mark missing actions NOTOBSERVED.
Preview approved source/device,provide printed TR1/TR4backup and record actual digital access separately.
Confirm40minute project/final pacing,target/tool capacity,accessibility and further performance opportunities.

lesson_map.title: Which angle gives a side its name?
Why do similar triangles give the same ratios?
What changes when a calculator uses degrees?
Why does sine match complementary cosine?
Which ratio connects the known and needed lengths?
Where does an elevation angle begin?
How does depression relate to elevation?
Can we build and calibrate a working clinometer?
What do repeated elevation and depression readings show?
What makes a real-life ratio claim useful?
Which trigonometry claims survive a labelled diagram?
